title: Osso Buco
subtitle: Braised cross-cut veal shin with gremolata
excerpt: Thick cross-cut pieces of veal shin braised slowly in white wine and stock until the bone-marrow is melting and the meat falls from the bone. Served with a sharp gremolata of lemon, garlic, and parsley.

recipe.sourceNotes: Osso buco (from the Milanese dialect for bone with a hole) is a Lombard dish of braised cross-cut veal shin, in which the bone and its central cavity of marrow form the centrepiece of the dish. The dish became a fixture of Milanese restaurant cooking in the nineteenth century and spread internationally during the twentieth. The traditional accompaniment is risotto alla milanese (saffron risotto), though creamy polenta or plain pasta are also traditional. The gremolata, a condiment of finely chopped lemon zest, garlic, and parsley, is added at the very end of cooking or at the table: its sharp, fresh flavour cuts through the richness of the braised meat. The bone marrow is considered a delicacy: it should be eaten directly from the bone with a small spoon. In the traditional recipe, no tomato is used; a more modern Milanese version includes tomato.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, deep casserole with a lid, large enough to hold the veal pieces in a single layer.

content.text: The veal pieces should be tied around the circumference with kitchen string before cooking: this stops the meat from falling off the bone during the long braise. Dust the pieces in flour and brown them cut-side first to develop colour at the marrow. The braising liquid should come no more than two-thirds up the sides of the veal: too much liquid means the sauce will be thin, and osso buco should have a concentrated, glossy sauce. Make the gremolata fresh just before serving.

items.preparation: 4 thick cross-cut pieces with the bone in, tied with string

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Dust the veal pieces in flour, shaking off the excess. Heat the oil in a wide casserole over high heat. Brown the veal for 3 minutes on each side until golden. Remove and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Soften the onion, carrot, and celery for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add the stock, thyme, and bay. Return the veal, standing the pieces upright.

Cover and braise in the oven for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours until the meat is very tender and just pulling from the bone. Remove the string. Mix the gremolata ingredients together. Serve the osso buco with the braising sauce spooned over and a scatter of gremolata.
